subject: Hip pointer
query: what is a hip pointer injury
title: What is a hip pointer injury? Football's painful hip bruise
answer: A hip pointer is a bruise, or contusion, on the upper outer part of the hip, caused by a direct blow to the iliac crest, the top ridge of the pelvis. It is common in contact sports such as football. Recovery usually takes one to three weeks, according to Norton Healthcare. ESPN reported that Giants QB J.J. McCarthy has one.
body:
Norton Healthcare says hip pointers often happen in contact sports but can also come from a fall. Symptoms include bruising, swelling and tenderness of the hip, limited range of motion and pain that can be severe and usually gets worse with activity.

Doctors advise getting checked to rule out a more serious injury. Standard care is rest, ice and compression as soon as possible; anti-inflammatory or pain medication may help, and gentle stretching can ease stiffness. If pain lasts more than a couple of weeks, Norton recommends seeing a doctor again.

Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the former Minnesota Vikings starter, hurt his hip in the Giants' win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported it was a hip pointer. Coach John Harbaugh said Monday that McCarthy was "doing well" and expected to play Thursday, Nov. 12, against the Washington Commanders.
in_the_news: Giants QB J.J. McCarthy is expected to play Nov. 12, 2026, despite a hip pointer suffered against the Eagles.

faq.q: What does a hip pointer feel like?
faq.a: Pain, tenderness, bruising and swelling over the top outer edge of the hip, with limited movement. The pain usually gets worse with activity.

faq.q: How long does a hip pointer take to heal?
faq.a: Usually one to three weeks, according to Norton Healthcare.
A direct hit to the iliac crest, the top of the pelvis, usually in contact sports. A fall can also cause one.

faq.q: What is a hip pointer in football?
faq.a: A deep bruise to the top of the hip bone from a hard hit or a fall, which is why it is common in contact sports like football.
It is usually a bruise rather than a break, but it can be very painful. A doctor should rule out a more serious injury.
